newsitem.title: USA: Envirodyne eyes sale of PVC film business.
newsitem.headline: Envirodyne eyes sale of PVC film business.

text.p: Envirodyne Industries Inc said Thursday it will explore the potential sale of its PVC flexible film business produced by its Viskase subsidiary.

It also said it will close its Sandusky Plastics injection molding plant in Sandusky, Ohio, and cease injection molded container product sales. Production is expected to end by May 1. Approximately 95 employees will be affected.
Envirodyne said selling its PVC business will enable its Viskase subsidiary to concentrate on building its global specialty film and casings business.
Involved in the sale are Viskase's plants in Aurora, Ohio and Sedgefield, England. Sales of Viskase PVC films in 1996 totaled $54.2 million.
Revenues generated from the sale of this business will be used to retire debt or for general corporate purposes.
Sandusky Plastics will concentrate its resources on development of its growing thermoforming business, which supplies plastic containers to the dairy, foodservice and horticulture markets.

Assets involved in Sandusky's injection molding plant will be transferred to Envirodyne's Clear Shield National subsidiary and will be used to manufacture plastic cutlery at Clear Shield's plant in Shreveport, La. and its recently announced new facility being built in Twin Falls, Idaho.
